title: Qwen4Exp 4K prefill is GPU-bound at 95.7%: the llama.cpp gap is pure kernel throughput, not scheduling
verdict: The prefill window is 95.7% GPU-busy, so no dispatch, scheduling, overlap or host-stall win is available. The 3.6x per-token gap to the tuned llama.cpp forks is a kernel-throughput gap and can only be closed by making kernels faster. This artifact is the priority map that directs that work.
quant: mixed GGUF: Q4_K gate/up experts, Q5_1 down experts, Q5_K 2 tensors, Q8_0 5 tensors
protocol: rocprofv3 --kernel-trace over scripts/qwen4exp_canonical_ar_bench.py prefill on code-p4096; raw trace at /tmp/repair-trace/raw-1.0/trace_kernel_trace.csv (85,696 launches). Traced under the promoted 1.0 binding; the 4.0 arm was traced identically and every share agrees within 0.15 points.

target_context.same_file_same_host_table: benchmarks/README.md 'Same-file prefill against every llama.cpp-family engine'
target_context.note: The tuned forks ramp 479.4 -> 860.8 -> 1051.6 across 512/1K/4K while hipEngine is flat-to-worse (294.5 -> 292.0 -> 259.6), so the gap is per-token cost rather than fixed overhead.

occupancy.setup_phase_gaps: 49 gaps of ~1 s, all in the first 49 s of weight upload and cache setup, adjacent to __amd_rocclr_copyBuffer calls that themselves total only 5 ms across 2516 dispatches

what_this_rules_out: Dispatch or launch overhead: 85,245 gaps under 50 ms total 1.364 s, a 0.016 ms median. Kernel launch overhead is not the gap.
Host-side stalls or a Python/ctypes bottleneck inside the prefill: the prefill window is 95.7% busy.
Overlap, stream-parallelism or scheduling wins: there is almost no idle time in the measured window to recover.
The 49 one-second stalls are real but are entirely outside the measured prefill window, in weight upload and cache setup. They affect time-to-first-token, not prefill throughput.
priority_reading: Ranked by absolute seconds available, the top four families are 64.08% of prefill. The MoE pair alone is 31.91% and its repair pass is a further 6.43%. A 3.6x per-token improvement - what matching the tuned forks requires - cannot come from a single family: it needs the top four to improve roughly in proportion.

known_levers_and_their_status.status: CLOSED - gate run and rejected: numerical_passed false, task_passed false, mixed_ja_en mean KL 1.499e-3 against the 1e-3 limit, broad-based drift rather than a tail artifact. The dense sibling with the identical mechanism failed the same way. benchmarks/results/2026-09-29-qwen4exp-hc1-gr-staged-gate/

known_levers_and_their_status.lever: remove the iu8 risk path via an F16 gate/up owner (MX-1)
known_levers_and_their_status.status: CLOSED - refuted on both halves: the F16 owner is 1.54-2.42x the production iu8-risk kernel, so the 1219.978 ms repair it would remove cannot pay for it, and it fails the production numerical envelope.
OPEN - measured 1.25x waste (12,800 padded rows for 10,240 real), worth roughly 4.1% of prefill on the gate/up half plus 2.3% on the down half if fully removed.

PARTIAL - the threshold is promoted (1.0, committed a0d705484) and the queue falls 3.403x, but fitting time = F + k*queue leaves F = 2794.1 ms fixed, 4.30% of the prefill window, which survives the promotion unchanged.
CLOSED - refuted as an occupancy loss: VGPR 72/130/256 and 28/15/8 waves per CU at widths 4/8/16, so 130 VGPR crosses the 128 granule and halves resident waves. Measures 0.833-0.844x.

limits: One host, one model file, one quant, one execution profile, one case (code-p4096).
Shares are from a single trace; the two binding arms agree within 0.15 points, which bounds arm-to-arm drift but not run-to-run drift.

rocprofv3 perturbs absolute timing, so this artifact is used for SHARES and occupancy rather than as a throughput measurement. The throughput numbers quoted for the comparison come from the canonical profiler-free protocol.
The per-launch counts reflect the harness's chunking, so ms/launch is a property of this chunk size rather than of the kernel alone.
